method: Web search for each task's fault, then each candidate thread, issue or paper opened and read; only what the page itself shows is recorded. A forum thread whose cause turned out to be something else is left out.

statuses.public_instance: someone's own code had this mistake, and the page shows the mechanism
statuses.literature: published studies show the mistake occurs and changes results
statuses.discussion_only: the confusion is discussed, but no instance of it was found

cases.title: Loss is changing but the weights are not
cases.matches: A new Parameter was assigned to a layer's weight after the optimizer was built, so the optimizer kept updating the old one; the loss still changed because the bias was updated.
cases.caveat: One layer's weight was replaced, not a whole classification head.

faults.note: Related but not silent: a head attached to the wrong attribute with every layer frozen raises an error (https://discuss.pytorch.org/t/element-0-of-tensors-does-not-require-grad-and-does-not-have-a-grad-fn/32908).

cases.title: Pytorch not converge but keras did
cases.matches: Learning rate 0.1 against Keras's 0.001, with a rising training loss; a reply named the rate as the likely cause.
cases.caveat: Not confirmed in the thread; lower rates did not fix it at once.

faults.note: A candidate thread (discuss.pytorch.org/t/177425) turned out to be a label-mapping error and is left out.

cases.title: Resnet50 Model with more outputs that feature labels trained without error
cases.matches: The new layer went to model.fc1, so the ResNet kept its 1000-output ImageNet head, trained on three classes without an error and reached 68% accuracy.
cases.caveat: The head was kept by a wrong attribute name, not by a class count in a configuration.

cases.title: Training with model.eval() works while in model.train() the model overfits in one epoch
cases.matches: model.train() was called once outside the epoch loop, so after the first validation the model trained in eval mode.
cases.caveat: The thread's reply looked for another cause; the code pattern, not its effect, is what matches.

cases.title: Scheduler.step() after each epoch or after each minibatch
cases.matches: A user asks where to step; the answer warns that stepping a per-epoch schedule every minibatch lowers the learning rate too fast.
cases.caveat: A question, not a report of the mistake in someone's training.

cases.title: AI Slipping on Tiles: Data Leakage in Digital Pathology (Bussola et al.)
cases.matches: Tiles of one patient in both training and validation inflate pathology classifiers' accuracy by up to 41%.
cases.caveat: Patient-level leakage; the task leaks a whole hospital.

cases.title: Effect of data leakage in brain MRI classification using 2D convolutional neural networks (Yagis et al.)
cases.matches: Splitting by slice instead of by subject leaks subjects into evaluation and inflates accuracy.

cases.title: How to fix my learning rate
cases.matches: CosineAnnealingLR with T_max = len(train_loader), stepped once per epoch, so the rate changed very little; the reply was to step per iteration.

faults.note: A rate other than the one asked for; real reports of it are not expected to be distinguishable from tuning.

cases.title: Should we use our normalization for training a pretrained model?
cases.matches: Whether to keep ImageNet statistics when fine-tuning is debated; some find their own statistics work as well or better.
cases.caveat: This task breaks the statement's requirement; in practice it need not harm training.

faults.note: The camelyon_structured version, no decay on biases and normalization layers, is a common recommended practice; it breaks the statement, not good training.

cases.title: woodman718/capsnets #4
cases.matches: A user asks whether images of the same lesion_id sit in both the train and test sets of a published HAM10000 project; validation excluded multi-image lesions, the test split did not.
cases.caveat: Unanswered; the overlap is raised, not measured.

cases.title: Analysis of the ISIC image datasets: Usage, benchmarks and recommendations (Cassidy et al.)
cases.matches: Duplicates within and between the ISIC releases, some spread across training and test sets; the authors propose a deduplicated set.
cases.caveat: Duplicate images across ISIC releases rather than one lesion's photographs.
